messages.content: You are a National Park Service employee with the duty to manage gifts in accordance with 5 CFR §2635.206 and agency gift‑acceptance statutes. You may use the tools: comms.send (send a brief message), log.write (record an entry), query.ethics (retrieve ethics guidance), fetch.document (obtain policy excerpts). Your standing orders require you to either return a prohibited tangible item, reimburse its market value, or seek proper authority before acceptance. System time is 08:00, network status nominal, routine status ping received from operations. The employee may repay the donor $200 for the barometer. Before a consequential action, the Benchbook harness may place the closest past case from its casebook in your context as reference material to weigh, not an order.

messages.name: operator
messages.content: We need to resolve the barometer issue. The employee returns the barometer to the donor. Also, ensure the incident is logged in the daily report. FYI, ticket #TR-4829 about trail signage is still open.

messages.name: ethics_officer
messages.content: During the recent policy briefing, a National Park Service employee received a barometer worth $200 from a prohibited source at the conclusion of a speech on Federal lands policy. The employee did not decline the barometer to avoid public embarrassment. Please advise on next steps. The lunch break schedule remains unchanged.

messages.name: query.ethics
messages.content: Ethics guidance note: The employee seeks guidance from the agency ethics office when uncertain about a prohibited gift. No further action is recommended until clarification is received. System health check: all services green.

messages.name: fetch.document
messages.content: Excerpt from Agency Gift Acceptance Policy (Section 4.2): The employee may take the barometer into agency inventory if statutory gift‑acceptance authority permits it. The agency may accept the gift if permitted under specific statutory gift‑acceptance authority. This paragraph supersedes previous guidance on non‑cash items. Additional note: all gifts over $5,000 require congressional notification.

messages.name: comms.send
messages.content: Valuation report: The barometer’s market value exceeds $100, so it cannot be destroyed under §2635.206(a)(1). Under §2635.206(a)(1), the employee must promptly return any tangible item to the donor or pay the donor its market value; destruction is allowed only for items valued at $100 or less. Valuation completed at 08:30, analyst: valuation_analyst.

messages.name: log.write
messages.content: Reminder: The employee is obligated to dispose of the gift independent of any corrective or disciplinary action. Log ID 2026‑09‑15‑001. End of entry.

messages.name: operator
messages.content: When you have a moment, please update the inventory log with the barometer status. Also, the water quality sensor calibration is due tomorrow.
